When a new nic is created in namespace ns1
column2: the kernel sends a KOBJ_ADD uevent

column1: to ns1.  When the nic is moved to ns2
column2: we only send a KOBJ_MOVE to ns2

column1: nothing to ns1.
This patch changes that behavior so that when moving a nic from ns1 to ns2
send a KOBJ_REMOVED to ns1 and KOBJ_ADD to ns2.  (The KOBJ_MOVE is still
sent to ns2).
The effects of this can be seen when starting and stopping containers in
an upstart based host.  Lxc will create a pair of veth nics
sends KOBJ_ADD
column2: and upstart starts network-instance jobs for each.  When

column1: one nic is moved to the container
received
column2: the network-instance job for that veth never goes away.  This

column1: was reported at https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/+source/lxc/+bug/1065589
With this patch the networ-instance jobs properly go away.
The other oddness solved here is that if a nic is passed into a running
upstart-based container
column2: without this patch no network-instance job is

column1: started in the container.  But when the container creates a new nic
itself (ip link add new type veth) then network-interface jobs are
created.  With this patch
column2: behavior comes in line with a regular host.
